title: The Prefix Nebe-
summary: Simple *ne-* denies a state; **nebe-** denies that the state still holds — *no longer / not anymore*. Its positive counterpart is **tebe-** (*still*), and both sit in the same slot as *ne-* relative to the stem and to reflexive *-si-*.

rules.heading: Nebe- Means No Longer
rules.statement: The prefix **nebe-** marks a **discontinuative**: the situation held before, and it does **not** hold now. English usually says *no longer* or *not anymore*; Lithuanian writes the idea onto the verb as one word — *nebedirbu*, *nebegaliu*, *nebelyja*. It is not a stronger form of ordinary *ne-* (¶25): *nedirbu* is *I do not work* (at this time, or habitually), while *nebedirbu* is *I no longer work* (I used to, and have stopped).

examples.gloss: She can no longer come. / She is no longer able to come.
It is no longer raining today.

footnotes: Sources: Ambrazas (ed.), *Lithuanian Grammar* (Vilnius: Baltos lankos, 1997), on the outer verbal prefixes; P. Arkadiev, “Typological peculiarities of Lithuanian verbal morphosyntax” (SLE 2010), glossing *ne-be-* as ‘no longer’ against *te-be-* ‘still’; school morphology (Keinys; Šukys; Paulauskienė) stating that *nebe-* marks an action that has been interrupted and is no longer performed (*nebeateiti, nebelyti, nebenorėti*).

rules.heading: How Nebe- Is Built and Written
rules.statement: **Nebe-** is historically **ne-** + the continuative element **be-** (‘still’): literally *not-still*. In the modern standard it is treated as **one** prefix written **together** with the verb (and with adjectives and adjectival adverbs formed the same way): *nebegaliu*, *nebegeras*, *nebetoli*. It is written **apart** from nouns, pronouns, numerals, and from those adverbs that also take separate *ne*: *nebe laikas*, *nebe tas*, *nebe vienas*. Under **contrast** (*not X, but Y*) it is likewise separate: *Nebe skaito, o rašo.*

examples.gloss: He is no longer good / kind.
It is no longer time to sleep.
He is no longer reading, but writing.

paradigms.caption: nebe- on a finite verb (dirbti)
paradigms.footnote: Tense and person endings are unchanged; only the prefix differs.

footnotes: Sources: N. Ostrowski, “Lithuanian discontinuatives *nebe-* / *jau nebe-* …”, *Folia Scandinavica* 20 (2016), deriving *nebe-* from outer negation *ne* + continuative *be(-)* ‘still’; official school orthography (eMokykla *Dalelyčių rašyba*; VLKK practice as taught in secondary curricula) — *nebe* with verbs/adjectives/adjectival adverbs together, with nouns/pronouns/numerals apart, and apart under contrast (*Nebe skaito, o rašo*).

rules.heading: Nebe- against Dar Ne- and Jau Ne-
rules.statement: Lithuanian has two ordinary ways of saying *no longer*, and they must not be confused with *not yet*. **Dar** + **ne-** (*dar nedirba*) is *still not / not yet*. **Jau** + **ne-** (*jau nedirba*) is the *already-not* discontinuative — *no longer*, built with the particle *jau* of ¶111. **Nebe-** (*nebedirba*) is the prefixed discontinuative of the same meaning, interchangeable with *jau ne-* in the standard language. The four-way square with the particles of ¶111 is therefore: *dar* ‘still’, *dar ne-* ‘not yet’, *jau* ‘already’, *jau ne-* / *nebe-* ‘no longer’.

examples.gloss: He is not working yet. / He still does not work.

paradigms.caption: Phasal square (dirbti, 3rd person)
paradigms.footnote: *Jau nebedirba* also occurs as an emphatic ‘already no longer’ (Ostrowski’s *jau nebe-*).

footnotes: Source: Ostrowski (2016), §§1–2 — the pan-Lithuanian inchoative discontinuative *jau ne-*, the West-Aukštaitian / standard prefixed discontinuative *nebe-*, their interchangeability in the literary language, and the Slavic-like square *dar / dar ne / jau / jau ne*. Do not invent a difference of ‘strength’ between *jau nedirba* and *nebedirba*; both mean *no longer*.

rules.heading: The Positive Counterpart Tebe-
rules.statement: The continuative partner of **nebe-** in modern standard Lithuanian is **tebe-**: *tebedirba* ‘is still working’, *tebelyja* ‘is still raining’. Where *dar* is a free particle (*jis dar dirba*), *tebe-* is a **prefix** written on the verb like *nebe-*. At A2 it is enough to **recognise** *tebe-* as ‘still’ on the verb and to **produce** *nebe-* for ‘no longer’; *dar* remains the everyday particle already learnt.

examples.gloss: Do you still live in Vilnius?

footnotes: Sources: Arkadiev (2010), examples of *te-be-* ‘still’ vs *ne-be-* ‘no longer’ as a typologically rare morphological encoding of phasal meanings; Ostrowski (2016), noting that *tebe-* superseded older continuative *be(-)* in the standard. Wikipedia-style sketches that invent other senses for *be-* without a grammar behind them are not used here.

rules.heading: Case, Reflexives, and Stacking
rules.statement: Everything that holds for **ne-** holds for **nebe-**. A transitive verb with *nebe-* still takes the **genitive of negation** (¶26): *nebeturi laiko*, not *nebeturi laiką*. On a **reflexive** verb the affix **-si-** stands **after** the outer prefix, as after *ne-* (¶157): *mokausi → nesimokau → nebesimokau*. *Nebe-* (like *ne-*, *te-*, *be-*, *tebe-*) may stand **outside** a lexical prefix: *nebeatvažiuoja* ‘no longer arrives’. Do not write a space inside the verb, and do not stack a second *ne-* beside *nebe-*.
footnotes: Sources: the genitive after negation is Ambrazas (1997) and ¶26 of this course; reflexive migration after outer prefixes including *nebe-* is the same rule as Ambrazas / standard descriptions summarised in Arkadiev and in the A1–A2 reflexive sections (*nesimokau*, *nebesimokau*); co-occurrence of *ne- / te- / be- / nebe- / tebe-* outside lexical prefixes is the standard inventory of ‘external’ prefixes (Arkadiev, “External verbal prefixes in Lithuanian”).

vocabulary.notes: Written together with verbs: nebedirbu. Contrast dar ne- (not yet).
Positive counterpart of nebe-: tebedirba ‘is still working’.

drills.stem: Complete: **Aš ______ čia.** (I no longer work here.)
drills.explanation: *Nebedirbu* = no longer work. *Nedirbu* is plain negation; *dar nedirbu* is not yet; *tebedirbu* is still working.

drills.stem: **Nebe-** is historically:
drills.explanation: Ostrowski: *nebe-* joins outer negation *ne* with continuative *be(-)* ‘still’.

drills.stem: Complete: **Jis ______.** (He is not working yet.)
drills.explanation: *Dar nedirba* = not yet / still does not. *Nebedirba* and *jau nedirba* mean no longer; *tebedirba* means still does.

drills.stem: Which correctly mean *no longer works* in the standard language?
drills.explanation: *Nebe-* and *jau ne-* are interchangeable discontinuatives. *Dar nedirba* is not yet; *tebedirba* is still.

drills.stem: Complete: **Jis ______ Vilniuje.** (He still lives in Vilnius — prefixed form.)
drills.explanation: *Tebe-* is the prefixed ‘still’. *Nebe-* would be no longer; *dar negyvena* is not yet living there.

drills.stem: Complete: **Jis nebeturi ______.**
drills.explanation: Genitive of negation holds under *nebe-* exactly as under *ne-*: *laiko*, not accusative *laiką*.

drills.stem: The correct form of *I no longer study* (*mokytis*) is:
drills.explanation: Outer *nebe-* then *-si-* then the stem: *nebesimokau*. Leaving *-si* at the end (*nebemokausi*) is the classic error; *nesimokau* is plain ‘I do not study’.

drills.stem: Which are written **together** as one word?
drills.explanation: Together with verbs and adjectives; apart before nouns (*nebe laikas*) and under contrast (*Nebe skaito, o rašo*).

drills.stem: In the phasal square *dar / dar ne / jau / jau ne≈nebe*, how many cells mean **no longer**?
drills.explanation: One meaning, two writings: *jau ne-* and *nebe-* occupy the same discontinuative cell.

drills.stem: Complete: **Šiandien ______.** (It is no longer raining.)
drills.explanation: *Nebelyja* = no longer raining. *Nelyja* is plain ‘is not raining’; *dar nelyja* is ‘is not raining yet’; *tebelyja* is ‘is still raining’.

drills.stem: About **nebe-** and **tebe-**, which are true?
options: *nebe-* means the situation no longer holds
*nebe-* is only used in the past tense
*tebe-* is the free particle *dar* written twice
drills.explanation: They are outer prefixes for ‘no longer’ and ‘still’, usable in any tense. *Dar* remains a separate particle.

drills.stem: Complete: **Jis ______.** (He no longer arrives / comes by vehicle.)
drills.explanation: External *nebe-* stands **outside** the lexical prefix *at-*: *nebeatvažiuoja*. It is not inserted inside the stem.

drills.stem: Complete: **Aš ______ kavos.** (I no longer want coffee.)
drills.explanation: *Nebenoriu* = no longer want. Genitive *kavos* follows from negation of *norėti*.

drills.stem: How many **external** prefixes of the set *ne-, te-, be-, nebe-, tebe-* appear in **jau nebesimokau**?
drills.explanation: One outer complex: *nebe-*. *Jau* is a free particle; *-si-* is the reflexive affix, not one of those five prefixes.

drills.title: Laiškas draugui
drills.passage:
Labas, Tomai.
Aš jau nebegyvenu Kaune — dabar esu Vilniuje. Dar nedirbu naujame darbe, bet tebegyvenu pas seserį. Seniau mokausi vokiečių kalbos, bet dabar nebesimokau: nebeturiu laiko. Jeigu atvažiuosi, parašyk. Nebeskambink vėlai vakare — miegame anksti.
Iki,
Rūta
drills.translation:
Hello, Tomas.
I no longer live in Kaunas — I am in Vilnius now. I am not working in the new job yet, but I am still living at my sister's. I used to study German, but I no longer study it: I no longer have time. If you come, write. Do not call late in the evening any more — we sleep early.
Bye,
Rūta

options: I no longer live in Kaunas
I do not yet live in Kaunas
questions.explanation: *Jau nebe-* is the emphatic discontinuative: no longer.

questions.stem: *Dar nedirbu* against *tebegyvenu* — which reading is right?
options: not working yet; still living (at the sister's)
no longer working; no longer living

questions.stem: Which forms in the letter correctly show **nebe-** + grammar already learnt?
questions.explanation: Reflexive migration, genitive of negation, and prefixed imperative are all real. Splitting *nebe-* from the verb is wrong.

questions.stem: How many **nebe-** verb forms appear in the letter?

drills.stem: Complete: **Mes ______ duonos.** (We no longer eat bread.)
drills.explanation: *Nebevalgome* + genitive *duonos*.

drills.stem: Which is the best gloss of **tebeaplanko**?
drills.explanation: *Tebe-* = still (Arkadiev’s *te-be-* continuative).

drills.stem: Complete: **______ pinigų.** Which fit *I no longer have money*?
drills.explanation: *Nebeturiu* and *jau neturiu* = no longer have (genitive *pinigų*). *Dar neturiu* = do not have yet; *tebeturiu* = still have.

drills.stem: Why is ***nebemokausi*** wrong for *I no longer study*?
options: Because *-si-* must stand after the outer prefix: *nebesimokau*
Because the verb must stay affirmative
drills.explanation: Same migration rule as *nesimokau*: prefix first, then *-si-*, then the personal form.

drills.stem: Complete: **Oras ______ šiltas.** (The weather is no longer warm — adjective.)
drills.explanation: With adjectives *nebe-* is written together: *nebešiltas*. (*Nebe šiltas, o šaltas* would be contrast with a space.)

drills.stem: Complete: **______ laikas eiti.** (It is no longer time to go — before a noun.)
drills.explanation: Before a noun *nebe* is a separate word: *Nebe laikas eiti.*

drills.stem: Which pairs are real antonyms on the verb?
drills.explanation: Prefixed *tebe-/nebe-* and the particle squares with *dar* and *jau* are all real. Plain *ne-* is not the dedicated partner of *tebe-*.

drills.stem: Complete: **Ji ______.** (She can no longer.)
drills.explanation: *Nebegali* — one word. *Dar negali* would be ‘cannot yet’.

drills.stem: In Ostrowski’s terms, *Jonas nebeturi laiko* paraphrases as:
options: It is not true that Jonas still has time
It is not true that Jonas already has time
Jonas has time but denies it politely
drills.explanation: Outer negation over continuative *be-*: ¬(still p) = no longer p.

drills.stem: Complete: **______ namie.** Which mean *He no longer is at home / does not live at home any more* with a verb of living or being?
drills.explanation: *Nebe-* and *jau ne-* = no longer. *Dar negyvena* = does not live there yet; *tebe-* = still.
